lesson_title: Seven Habits of an Honest Till
hook_text: The electrician offers two prices — one with paper, one without. What exactly is that cheaper price buying?
clip_script: Two prices. With an invoice, or cheaper — cash, no paperwork. Feels like a discount, but look at what is being sold off. Transparency: the deal is DESIGNED to leave no trace. Accountability: no record means nobody can ever be held to anything — including when the wiring fails. And fairness, quietly, downstream: untaxed cash work shifts the burden onto everyone who declares honestly. This is what ethics questions actually test — not 'is it wrong', your gut already knows. The skill is naming WHICH characteristic is under attack, and arguing it. Seven characteristics run every honest business: leadership, discipline, transparency, accountability, fairness, sustainability, responsible management. Learn to spot them at the till, and the marks follow.
visual_style: Split-screen: two handwritten quotes, one stamped INVOICE and one dissolving into smoke; characteristic names slam on screen as each is traded away.
pacing: Fast hook on the two prices, three quick reveals, rapid-fire list of the seven, punchy close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never lose an ethics mark again.
